To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD133 and CD444 are both necessary for defining CSCs in HCC.

cancer stem cell (CSC) phenotype could be precisely characterized by the co‐expression of cell surface markers CD133 and CD4, and that CD133+ CD44+ cells are highly tumorigenic in vivo, and exhibit extensive self‐renewability, differentiation, and chemoresistance.

CD133+ cells, which were previously identified as cancer stem cells in HCC by our previous study, could be more precisely defined by coexpression of CD133+CD133+CD44+, which showed stem cell properties and were more tumorigenic in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cancer stem cells in HCC and the molecular mechanism underlying the resistance of cancer stem cells to chemotherapy.
the isolation and characterization of cancer stem cells, which are enriched in a CD133+CD4+ population in hepatoma cells.
the study of the stem cells in hepatocellular carcinomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD133+ cells in HCC represent the tumor‐initiating cell subpopulation, but not the entire population.
CD133+ cells are enriched with CSCs in HCC.

CD133+ cells in HCC represent a heterogeneous cell population, including CD133+CD34−CD44−, CD133+CD45−CD44− cells, as well as a small subpopulation of CD133+CD24+CD44+, which are the true cancer stem cells, and CD133+CD31+CD44+ which are endothelial progenitor cells, while CD133+CD26+CD44−, which is the main component, is a progenitor cell
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD133+CD34+ cell population is a more reliable cancer stem cell (CSC) marker than CD133+CD24− cell population for hepatocellular carcinoma, and CD133+CD133+ cell population is not a CSC marker.
the CD133+CD133−CD44−CD44+ subpopulation is a more appropriate marker for CSCs in HCC.

CD133+ cells in hepatocellular carcinomas could be further divided into two subpopulations, namely CD133+CD133−CD44+ cells and CD133+CD13+CD44− cells, with the former being more highly tumorigenic than the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD133+CD34+ population of HCC cells is enriched for CSCs.
CD133+ and CD44+ cells in HCC could be regarded as cancer stem cells, which may be useful in future research on the development of novel therapeutic strategies against HCC.
CD133+ cells in HCC might be a mixed cell population, including CSCs and other cancer cell types.
